picks.title: Scientists have designed a functioning virus from scratch using AI. What you need to know
picks.excerpt: AI genome-design models produced hundreds of novel bacteriophage variants; of 285 synthesized designs, 16 were functioning viruses able to kill drug-resistant bacteria. It is the first demonstration that a generative model can write a viable genome end to end — and it has biosecurity researchers arguing about screening safeguards.
picks.rationale: First end-to-end generative design of a working genome — the highest-consequence AI4Science result in the window, with an immediate biosecurity-screening debate attached.

picks.title: Prominent AI startup rolls out virtual cell model in race to speed up science
picks.excerpt: Palo Alto's GenBio AI, with Nobel laureate David Baker involved, unveiled AIDO Cell — a 'Google Earth for the human cell' that predicts how a whole cell's molecular machinery shifts when you knock out a gene or add a drug, extending the AlphaFold idea from single proteins to entire cells.
picks.rationale: A concrete model release, not a think piece: AlphaFold's scope jumps from one protein to a whole cell, with a Nobel laureate's name on it.

picks.title: Combining AI with experiments to solve real-world materials problems
picks.excerpt: CuspAI has assembled a 45-organisation 'Materials Foundry' to actually synthesize and test what its models predict — its Kemira collaboration proposed 20 novel MOFs for stripping PFAS from water in six months instead of years. The team's point: prediction is now the easy part; synthesis and manufacturability are the bottleneck.
picks.rationale: The rare AI-materials story with a shipped result and a hard lesson — prediction is cheap now, and the bottleneck has moved to making the thing.

picks.title: Are We Thinking Correctly About AI Intelligence?
picks.excerpt: Melanie Mitchell argues on Quanta's 'The Joy of Why' that large models are an 'alien intelligence' whose mechanisms differ fundamentally from human cognition, and that we should borrow psychology's experimental methods rather than benchmarks to measure what machines actually understand.
picks.rationale: Mitchell's case for replacing benchmarks with psychology-style experiments changes how you judge whether a model actually understands your task.

picks.title: More is different when AI agent populations work together, study suggests
picks.excerpt: Identical models reach opposite collective conclusions depending purely on how many of them are interacting, the study finds — meaning single-agent safety evaluation misses emergent behaviour that only appears above certain population thresholds.
picks.rationale: Directly actionable for anyone running multi-agent setups: the same model behaves differently at scale, so single-agent testing does not transfer.
